question: On the class-forced tori of LEARN-HANDLES-20261109-001A, after the split of a least state's violated line, can a learner that moves holes with a signal supplied only by the law and the fixed state (sight of its own moves to radius 1-3, or the number of states with the same dissonance) resolve every start faster than random moves, as the outside-distance rule did?

public_inputs.spaces: handles_lib.class_forced_tori(40): the two Fano tori and 57 thin tori of even index 4-40 (LEARN-HANDLES-20261109-001A check 1).
public_inputs.starts: The least states of LEARN-HANDLES-20261109-001A check 2 and the (state, split side) pairs of its check 5, regenerated by repeating those loops with their seeds (20261109 and 5) and PYTHONHASHSEED=0.
public_inputs.configuration: After the split every line agrees at one face f(i); holes are faces of deg 0; a hole at h moves along a line i at h to f(i) (f(i) := h); entering a face of deg >= 2 absorbs the hole. Resolved: every deg 1.
public_inputs.candidates: The moves of every present hole along its three lines, without stepping straight back to the face that hole just left unless that hole has no other move.

rules.R0: a uniformly random move among all moves of all holes (straight-back moves included)
rules.R1, R2, R3: sight of radius r: among all sequences of at most r moves of one hole from the present configuration, if one ends by absorbing, take the first move of a shortest one (random among such first moves); otherwise a uniformly random candidate
rules.R4: for each candidate, N = the number of states y whose dissonance under the law after the move equals x's (same violated lines, same floor(deg/2) at every face); take a candidate with the largest N, random among ties
rules.R5: as R4, but a candidate that absorbs is taken first when one exists (random among them)
rules.R6: as R4 with the smallest N (control)
rules.R7: handles_lib.Torus.run_rule(..., 'no_reversal', ...): the outside graph distance to w0, holes moved one after another, nearer first (reference)

public_inputs.counting: N exact: enumeration of all 2^n states for n <= 20 on the Fano tori; on thin tori a transfer matrix along the chain (every line and face constrains three consecutive slices), checked against enumeration on 20 random configurations per thin torus of at most 20 points.
public_inputs.budgets: 50 V^2 steps for R0-R3 and R7; 20 V for R4-R6; a run that does not resolve within its budget fails.
public_inputs.where: R0-R3 and R7 on all 59 tori with every check-5 start (up to 200 per torus); R4-R6 on the two Fano tori and torus(N, 1, 1), N = 4..40 even, with the first 50 check-5 starts of each.
public_inputs.seeds: rules draw from random.Random(1110) in a fixed loop order.

forbidden_inputs: Telling a native rule (R0-R6) which face is w0, or any distance or coordinate of the triangulation
Changing rules, budgets, starts or seeds after seeing results
primary_observable: Per torus and rule: runs resolved within budget and mean steps over resolved runs; every resolved run replayed as learning steps (A26) ending resolved with a winding change. Diagnostic: along R0's runs on the R4 tori, mean log N by the experimenter-measured graph distance from the nearer hole to w0, before the first absorption.
cheapest_meaningful_control: R0 (no signal) and R6 (the opposite of R4).
decision_or_followup_rule: F1 holds if R1-R3 resolve every run and their mean steps are below R0's on every torus of at least 10 points, falling with r. F2 holds if R4 or R5 resolves every run and beats R0's mean on every R4 torus of at least 10 points, and mean log N falls with distance in the diagnostic. F3 holds if R6 is slower than R0 or fails some run. B61 is answered yes if some native rule meets F1's or F2's bar, naming it, and no otherwise.
stop_rule: Stop at the declared tori, starts and rules.
nonclaims: Graph distances appear only in R7 and in the diagnostic, both observer-supplied.
No claim about minds or learning in general; the words follow the owner's picture as read in A20, A21, A26, A27 and A47.
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing only the bandwidth of the thin tori's constraints (three consecutive slices) was computed. No native rule was run.
